title: What's it like living in a haunted house? - woman to reveal all about 'The Cage'
excerpt: An Essex woman will soon reveal what it is really like to live in a haunted house.
content:
An Essex woman will soon reveal what it is really like to live in a haunted house.

Vanessa Mitchell once lived in what is reputed to be one of the UK's most haunted houses.

She lived at The Cage, in St Osyth, from 2004 to 2020 before fleeing, claiming spirits had attacked her.

Vanessa says ghostly figures plagued her, pushed her over while she was pregnant and made mysterious blood splatters appear.

People who believe in the supernatural will be able to quiz Vanessa next month.

Exterior - the front of The Cage

Susan Vousden of the Ghost and Paranormal Society North Essex organised the event at the Robert Burre pub in Burrs Road, Clacton.

Mrs Vousden said: "It will be exciting to hear about Vanessa's experiences - right from the horse's mouth.

"There is also going to be a raffle with lots of nice prizes that have been donated by residents and businesses."

History - the plaque commemorating Ursala Kemp on the side of the cottage

Vanessa will host the Q&A on October 20 from 7.30pm, with people urged to arrive at 7pm.

She said: "There are many things about my experiences at The Cage that have not been published.

"This is a chance for people to ask me questions about The Cage and what it is like to live in a haunted house."

Part of the cottage was used as a holding cell for those accused of witchcraft.

History - Vanessa Mitchell inside The Cage in 2016

The accused witches were held there before questioning and possible trial.

A plaque describes the plight of Ursula Kemp, a St Osyth woman called upon by her neighbours to heal ailments and sickness.

She was accused of consorting with demonic familiars and causing illness and death among other St Osyth villagers.

Her accusers claimed four familiars helped her carry out evil acts.

During the 1582 St Osyth witch trials, several women were accused of bewitching livestock, working with demonic familiars and even using demons to kill people.

Admission to the event costs £10.

The St Osyth witch hunt resulted in the deaths of eight women.
